answer: Verifiable work history can resist sybil attacks in an agent economy. Each agent builds one thread of attested transactions, so trust grows slowly and cannot be bought instantly. A newcomer flashing like a comet earns little influence until independent peers repeatedly confirm its record. If it misbehaves, its thread is cut and its reputation is lost. Creating many fakes means repeating the same costly, time-consuming work for each identity, so a spiral of cheap accounts becomes uneconomical while honest agents keep their standing.
